# /panel-ledger

## Purpose

Track every character and every object through the issue, panel by panel,
and prove the sequence is possible before it is drawn. The ledger lives in
the `cast`, `props`, and `transfers` of each panel in `page.yaml`. It
records where someone stands, what they wear, what state they are in, what
they hold, and how any of that changed since their last appearance. A
character who is out of frame keeps a row when their state matters, because
leaving the frame resets nothing.

## Use When

- Pages are scripted and no prompt has been compiled yet. This audit is a
  precondition of `/reference-plan` and `/generate-pages`.
- A page plan or a script changed after the ledger was filled.
- A review reported a `position`, `movement`, `object_custody`,
  `physical_state`, or `wardrobe` finding and the plan has to be checked
  before a repair.

## Inputs

- `issue` (ID, required): the `ISS_###` to track.
- `pages` (ID or range, optional): limit the editing to these pages. The
  audit always runs on the whole issue.
- `--check` (flag, optional): run the audit and report; edit nothing.

## Invokes Agents

- continuity-editor
- layout-artist

## Required Skills

- state-tracking
- scene-blocking

## Process

1. Load the opening state. If `issue.yaml` has `opens_from`, read that
   `production/continuity/<ISS_ID>.final-state.yaml`; otherwise take the
   starting positions from the scene's `geography.notes` and the story
   bible. Load the location maps, each `wardrobe.yaml`, and
   `hands_required` from each prop file.
2. Walk the panels of the issue in reading order. In every panel, write a
   `cast` row for each character whose state matters to the sequence. A
   character who is not drawn gets a row with `off_panel: true` and keeps
   their position, wardrobe, state, and whatever they hold.
3. Fill every row completely: `position` (`level`, `side`, `landmark`),
   `facing`, `action`, `wardrobe`, `state`, and `holding`. Set `carrying`
   when the character supports or carries another. Empty lists are written
   as empty lists; a missing field is an unknown.
4. Account for each change against the character's previous appearance. A
   new level sets `moved` on the row or `ellipsis` on the panel. A state
   tag gained or lost is declared in `state_changes.adds` or
   `state_changes.resolves`. A different outfit inside a scene sets
   `wardrobe_change`.
5. Track the objects. A prop in nobody's hands gets a `props` row with
   `position`, `state`, and `visible`. Each change of holder is a
   `transfers` entry in the panel where it happens: `prop`, `from`, `to`,
   and `how` (`handoff` | `pickup` | `drop` | `set_down` | `draw` |
   `holster` | `throw` | `take`).
6. Count hands. `carrying` takes two. Each held prop takes its
   `hands_required`. More than two hands in a row is an impossible panel.
7. Run `node scripts/check-continuity.js --root production --issue
   <ISS_ID>`. Read every finding: code, severity, page, panel, entity.
8. Fix each error in the plan. A custody error usually means a missing
   transfer or a missing panel; a level error means an unshown move.
   layout-artist adds the panel when one is needed and updates
   `layout.tiers` and `layout.reading_order`. An error is never waived, and
   a caption is never the fix for a handoff nobody drew.
9. Run the audit again until it reports zero errors. Read the warnings and
   either fix them or note why they stand in the panel's `notes`.
10. Run the self-evaluation gates on the page files and report: rows
    written, off-panel rows, transfers, and the audit result. Generation
    does not start while the audit has an error.

## Outputs

- `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/page.yaml`, with complete
  `cast`, `props`, and `transfers` in every panel; validates against
  `schemas/page.schema.json`.
- The audit report from `check-continuity.js`, in the conversation.

## Notes

- This command costs nothing, and each error it catches is a page that is
  not generated wrong.
- The audit is mechanical. It proves the plan is coherent; it says nothing
  about a rendered page. `/visual-review` compares the pixels with this
  ledger.
- The hook `detect-continuity-drift.js` warns when a later edit to a page
  file drifts from the ledger. It is advisory. Run this audit again after
  any change to the script or the layout.
- State tags follow the pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`. Use the same tag for
  the same thing across the issue (`cut_left_hand`, not three spellings of
  it).
- Escalate to the user when the only way to make a sequence possible is to
  change an event of the story.
- Related: `/panel-script` (before), `/reference-plan` and
  `/generate-pages` (gated by the audit), `/continuity-review` (the same
  discipline across pages and issues).
